messages:
Nina K: Started a PR to consolidate function-calling examples under the new structured-output schema. Main goals: clear SDK snippets (Python + Go), union/nullable examples, and a guardrails checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4501 :wave:
Omar V: Nice. Can you paste the Go SDK example? We haven't had many Go snippets in this section.
Nina K: Sure, added this minimal example for calling a tool and reading the new field:
```go
resp, _ := client.CallTool(ctx, "reranker", opts)
output := resp.ToolOutput // new canonical field
if output != nil { fmt.Println(output.Choices[0].Id) }
```
Ben S: Solid. I'll add a tiny Python example too that shows a safe accessor with fallback to old field:
```py
res = client.call_tool("summarize", payload)
output = getattr(res, "toolOutput", None) or res.tool_result
print(output.get("summary"))
```
Omar V: For the docs we should also show the union case: tool returns either {choices:[]} or {error:"..."}. I suggested a JSON schema snippet and a parse-fallback example that falls back to `raw_text` when validation fails.
Nina K: Added an inline union example and a small validator snippet in TypeScript for clarity:
```ts
function isChoices(obj:any): obj is {choices:any[]} { return Array.isArray(obj?.choices); }
let parsed = tryParse(responseText);
if (!isChoices(parsed)) parsed = { raw_text: responseText };
```
Ben S: I also included an example for nullable arrays and empty responses to show safe iteration patterns.
docs-lint-bot: lint check results: docs lint OK. Please fix one style nit in migration notes (use 'canonical' not 'primary').
link-scout: Link check failed: https://docs.redwood.ai/specs/tool-output-legacy -> 404.
Nina K: Thanks link-scout. Replaced link with canonical: https://docs.redwood.ai/schemas/structured-output-2025.json and updated PR.
Omar V: Under Guardrails I added recommended required fields for routing: `request_id` (string), `confidence` (0.0-1.0), and optional `diagnostics`. Also recommended small `example_response` block for typegen.
Ben S: One runtime question: is `confidence` guaranteed to be present for all tools? If not we should mark it optional in examples but recommend it for routing tools.
Omar V: It's recommended, not enforced. Marked optional in JSON schema snippets but called out as a strong recommendation in the guardrails note.
Nina K: Pushed updates: added Go + Python snippets, union & nullable examples, guardrails checklist, migration checklist with a single-line alias snippet: `const out = res.toolOutput ?? res.tool_result`.
docs-lint-bot: PR 4501 -> docs build preview ready: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/4501/docs/structured-output-migration.html
link-scout: Link check passed for updated URLs.
Ben S: LGTM. Maybe add an optional tiny example showing nested tool outputs (tool returns another tool's output) and how to flatten for SDKs. I'll drop that in a follow-up commit.
Nina K: Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge after one more docs review. Drop any extra edge-case examples here and I'll fold them in. :thumbsup:
